title: Small Artinian tests imply local square-zero lifting with nilpotent maximal ideal
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ and $(S,\mathfrak n)$ be commutative local rings and let $R\to S$ be a local homomorphism. Here local means having exactly one maximal ideal and a local homomorphism has inverse image of the target maximal ideal equal to the source maximal ideal. Suppose $S$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. A small extension is a surjection $B'\twoheadrightarrow B$ of commutative Artinian local rings whose kernel $I$ is nonzero, is annihilated by $\mathfrak m_{B'}$, and has dimension one as a vector space over $B'/\mathfrak m_{B'}$. Artinian means that every descending chain of ideals stabilizes. Assume that for every such small extension, every local map $R\to B'$, and every local $R$-algebra map $g:S\to B$ inducing an isomorphism $S/\mathfrak n\xrightarrow{\sim}B/\mathfrak m_B$, there is an $R$-algebra lift $g':S\to B'$ of $g$. Then for every commutative local $R$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ with local structure map and $\mathfrak m_A^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$, every ideal $J\subset A$ with $J^2=0$, and every local $R$-algebra map $v:S\to A/J$ inducing an isomorphism $S/\mathfrak n\xrightarrow{\sim}(A/J)/\mathfrak m_{A/J}$, there exists an $R$-algebra map $w:S\to A$ with $(A\to A/J)\circ w=v$. The test ring $A$ is not required to be Artinian or Noetherian.

proof.text: First reduce to kernels annihilated by the maximal ideal. Put $K_t=\mathfrak m_A^tJ$ for $0\leq t\leq N$ and $A_t=A/K_t$. Then $K_0=J$, $K_N=0$, and $A_{t+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_t$ has square-zero kernel $K_t/K_{t+1}$ annihilated by $\mathfrak m_{A_{t+1}}$. Each $K_t\subseteq J\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$, so these rings are local with the original residue field and nilpotent maximal ideal, and $R\to A_t$ is local. Indeed a unit modulo a square-zero ideal is a unit: if $xy=1+j$, then $y(1-j)$ is an inverse. Thus the inverse image of the maximal ideal under each quotient is the maximal ideal. Starting with $v:S\to A_0$, solve successively these $N$ lifting problems. Any lift is local and has the same residue isomorphism, because its composite with the quotient does. Consequently it suffices to solve every test problem with $\mathfrak m_AJ=0$. A zero kernel is immediate: use the inverse of the quotient isomorphism. In steps 2--6 assume $J\ne0$ and $\mathfrak m_AJ=0$.

proof.text: Write $q:A\to A/J$, $D=v(S)$, and $C=q^{-1}(D)\subseteq A$. The structure map from $R$ lands in $C$, and $C/J=D$. Let $L=\ker(v:S\to D)$. Locality gives $L\subseteq\mathfrak n$, while $\mathfrak n^N\subseteq L$ because $\mathfrak m_A^N=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] with ring $S$, ideal $L$, and exponent $N$: $D\cong S/L$ is Artinian local. Its residue field is $k=S/\mathfrak n$, identified with $A/\mathfrak m_A$ by the hypothesis. The ring $C$ is local with maximal ideal $C\cap\mathfrak m_A$: if $c$ has nonzero residue, its image in $D$ is invertible; lift that inverse to $b\in C$, write $cb=1+j$, and use $b(1-j)\in C$ as inverse. Its maximal ideal has $N$th power zero. Thus $R\to C$ is local, $S\to D$ is a local $R$-algebra map with residue isomorphism, and $\mathfrak m_CJ=0$. A lift to $C$ composed with $C\subseteq A$ solves the given problem. Hence from now on construct a lift for $S\to D=C/J$, retaining this $C$, $J$ and $k$.

source.place: Tag 0DYG (lemma-fs-local), proof of (3) implies (2), last paragraph; small extensions: algebra.tex Tag 02HS (definition-small-extension).

proof.text: The action of $C$ on $J$ factors through $k=C/\mathfrak m_C$, so $J$ is a $k$-vector space. Every $k$-subspace $H\subseteq J$ is a $C$-ideal. Let $\mathcal H$ be the set of subspaces with one-dimensional quotient $J/H$. They separate the elements of $J$. For $0\ne j\in J$, apply [lem-trf-vector-subspace-complement] to the line $kj\subseteq J$, obtaining $J=kj\oplus H$. Projection along $H$ identifies $J/H$ with $kj$, so $H\in\mathcal H$ and $j\notin H$. In particular $\mathcal H$ is nonempty and $\bigcap_{H\in\mathcal H}H=0$. No finite-dimensionality of $J$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0DYG (lemma-fs-local), proof of (3) implies (2), last paragraph; small extensions: algebra.tex Tag 02HS (definition-small-extension).

proof.text: For $H\in\mathcal H$ put $E_H=C/H$ and $U_H=J/H$. The quotient $E_H\to D$ is surjective with nonzero one-dimensional kernel $U_H$ annihilated by the maximal ideal. The ring $E_H$ is local with residue field $k$, since $H\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$ and units of $C$ descend. It is Artinian: in any descending chain of its ideals, the images in the Artinian ring $D$ stabilize, as do the intersections with the one-dimensional $k$-space $U_H$. For nested ideals $V'\subseteq V$ with equal images and equal intersections, any $x\in V$ has $y\in V'$ with the same image; then $x-y\in V\cap U_H=V'\cap U_H$, so $x\in V'$. The chain therefore stabilizes. Hence $E_H\twoheadrightarrow D$ is a small extension as defined in the statement. The maps $R\to E_H$ and $S\to D$ are local and the latter has residue isomorphism. The assumed small-extension test supplies a lift $f_H:S\to E_H$ over $R$. Choose such a lift for each $H$.

source.place: Tag 0DYG (lemma-fs-local), proof of (3) implies (2), last paragraph; small extensions: algebra.tex Tag 02HS (definition-small-extension).

proof.text: Form the ring $P$ of tuples $(e_H)_{H\in\mathcal H}\in\prod_HE_H$ whose images in $D$ all equal a single element. Operations are coordinatewise. Since $\mathcal H\ne\varnothing$, their common image defines a surjection $p:P\to D$: lift an element of $D$ first to $C$ and then take all its quotient images. The canonical map $i:C\to P$, $c\mapsto(c\bmod H)_H$, is injective. Indeed if $i(c)=0$, then $c\in J$ and $c\in H$ for every $H$, so step 3 gives $c=0$. Its restriction embeds $J$ into $J'=\ker p=\prod_H(J/H)$. This ideal has square zero. Coordinatewise multiplication shows that the action of $P$ on $J'$ is multiplication by the common residue in $k$: each $\mathfrak m_{E_H}$ annihilates $J/H$. In particular $J'$ is a $k$-vector space and $i|_J$ is $k$-linear. The tuple $f=(f_H)_H:S\to P$ is an $R$-algebra map, since every $f_H$ reduces to the same map $S\to D$; the structural $R$-map of $P$ is the composite $R\to C\xrightarrow{i}P$.

source.place: Tag 0DYG (lemma-fs-local), proof of (3) implies (2), last paragraph; small extensions: algebra.tex Tag 02HS (definition-small-extension).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-vector-subspace-complement] to the subspace $i(J)\subseteq J'$ to obtain $J'=i(J)\oplus M$. The subspace $M$ is an ideal of $P$, because the $P$-action on $J'$ is its residue scalar action. Every $e\in P$ has a unique expression $e=i(c)+m$ with $c\in C$ and $m\in M$. For existence, lift $p(e)$ to $c_0\in C$, and decompose $e-i(c_0)=i(j)+m$ in $J'$, giving $c=c_0+j$. For uniqueness, $i(c-c')\in M\subseteq J'$ forces $c-c'\in J$, and $i(J)\cap M=0$ with injectivity of $i$ gives $c=c'$. Define $\rho(e)=c$. Uniqueness makes $\rho$ additive, and $M$ being an ideal makes it multiplicative: $(i(c)+m)(i(d)+n)-i(cd)\in M$. It fixes $i(C)$, hence is unital and preserves the structural $R$-map. Moreover $q_C\rho=p$, where $q_C:C\to D$. Thus $\rho f:S\to C$, followed by $C\subseteq A$, lifts the original $v$ in the socle case. Apply this result successively to the finite tower in step 1 to obtain $w:S\to A$ for arbitrary $J$.

(1) The filtration m_A^t J ends at 0 because m_A^N=0; each kernel is square-zero and killed by m, and the unit trick (1+j)(1-j)=1 keeps every lift local with the residue isomorphism. (2) The hypotheses of lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local hold with K=ker v: n^N is in ker v and ker v is in n. The inverse-image subring C is local by the b(1-j) inverse. (3) The complement leaf has no finite-dimensionality assumption; the hyperplanes are C-ideals, separate J, and intersect to 0. (4) The Artinian proof for C/H holds: images in D and intersections with the one-dimensional kernel both stabilise. It is a small extension in the statement's sense and the hypothesis data match. (5) P is well defined, p is onto, i is injective, ker p is a square-zero k-space, and the tuple of lifts is an R-algebra map into P. (6) The complement M is an ideal, the decomposition i(c)+m exists and is unique, and rho is a ring retraction with q_C rho=p. Edge cases checked: J=0, N=1, dim J=1, infinite-dimensional J with A not Artinian, mixed characteristic.
